top_stories.title: Over 41,000 DHS Employee Records Leaked Online
top_stories.summary: Over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employee records were leaked online after allegedly being stolen from an Okta single sign-on system. The breach exposed both personal and work information of DHS employees.

top_stories.title: Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data
top_stories.summary: Attackers impersonated IT support via Microsoft Teams to gain remote access to employee devices, then exploited misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) to obtain login certificates for privileged accounts including domain controllers. Microsoft investigated two such intrusions, with at least one resulting in data theft from the compromised organization.

top_stories.title: DHS: 41,000+ Employee Records Leaked Online, Along With a Map of What Each Account Can Open
top_stories.summary: A threat actor published a database containing personal and work details of over 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The leaked data reportedly includes a map of what each account can access, exposing access control and authorization structures across DHS systems.

top_stories.title: Opal’s agent.ID virtual event: Top security leaders on governing Al agents
top_stories.summary: Opal Security is hosting agent.ID, a free virtual event on November 5, 2026, focused on IAM for AI agents. The event will feature CISOs and identity leaders from companies including Elastic, Instacart, and Databricks, covering topics such as non-human identity access reviews, just-in-time access, and AI agent governance.

top_stories.title: CISA to federal agencies: Remediate exploited Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527)
top_stories.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, directing federal agencies to remediate them. The flaws include a missing authentication vulnerability enabling local privilege escalation and a predictable identifier vulnerability allowing remote authenticated file upload, with three flaws reportedly chained together to gain initial access.

news.title: Stolen AI access leaves companies with cloud bills of up to $1 million
news.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant researchers found that criminals are breaking into corporate cloud accounts and using stolen access credentials to run AI models at victims' expense, a technique called LLMJacking. In documented incidents from 2026, attackers generated over $100,000 in charges in a single day, targeting financial services, retail, and technology sectors.

news.title: Phishing-resistant MFA where it matters most, and finding the privileged identities your role report misses
news.summary: The article provides guidance on implementing phishing-resistant MFA and passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID, focusing specifically on administrator accounts and privileged identities. It is part six of a seven-part series, covering how to identify privileged identities that may be missed in standard role reports.

news.title: Chainalysis Confirms Intrusion Into Internal Tools and Exposure of Customer Identity Data
news.summary: Chainalysis confirmed a cybersecurity incident in which an external actor accessed non-sensitive customer identity data through internal tools. The company stated that authentication credentials and session tokens were not compromised in the breach.

news.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
news.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation in the wild. The flaws, including CVE-2026-111357 (CVSS 8.8), a missing authentication vulnerability, are being chained with a third flaw to achieve unauthenticated root access on affected systems.

news.title: Okta jumps after-hours following tapped inclusion in the S&P 500
news.summary: Okta has been selected by S&P Dow Jones Indices to join the S&P 500 benchmark index. The announcement caused Okta shares to climb 2.1% in after-hours trading.

news.title: Okta Set to Join S&P 500; Others to Join S&P MidCap 400 and S&P SmallCap 600
news.summary: Okta Inc. is set to join the S&P 500 index, moving up from the S&P MidCap 400, effective prior to market open on November 4. This index inclusion reflects Okta's market capitalization growth and elevates its profile among large-cap publicly traded companies.

news.title: Implement least-privilege access with designations in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio has introduced a feature called "designations," which are named permission sets enabling granular, least-privilege access control for project members. The feature allows administrators to define and assign specific permissions to users within SageMaker projects.

news.title: $38.4 bn market cap: DHS Data leak details - Okta says its core systems not compromised | All you need about company
news.summary: A data leak reportedly exposing personal and job details of more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees is under investigation, with Distributed Denial of Secrets claiming the data came through Okta. Okta has stated it found no evidence that its core systems or infrastructure were compromised in connection with the incident.

news.title: Hackers steal and publish data on 41,000 Homeland Security workers
news.summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen and published data on 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees. The exposed data includes work contact details and internal group memberships, raising concerns about identity exposure and access-related information.

news.title: Hackers leak personnel data of 41,000+ Homeland Security staff, including ICE and border agents
news.summary: Hackers leaked personal data of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including ICE and CBP agents. The breach exposed staff personnel details, which were subsequently published online.

news.title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees
news.summary: A hacktivist group published the work details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including names, titles, and phone numbers. The data was reportedly extracted from a login system, making this directly relevant to IAM professionals from an authentication and access system security perspective.
